title: The bottom Grothendieck edge is homology of the derived single unit
statement: Let A and B be Grothendieck abelian categories and C abelian, with bounded-below derived categories. Let F:A→B and G:B→C be additive, with F left exact [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. For X in A and n≥0, identify the source of the raw bottom Grothendieck edge [lem-sp-grothendieck-edge-maps] with R^nG(FX). The identified edge equals the inverse single-object homology comparison for G [lem-sp-derived-well-defined], followed by H^n(RG(u_F(X))), where u_F(X):F(X)[0]→RF(X) is rightDerivedPlusSingleUnit from [lem-sbc-right-derived-single-unit-homology-comparison]. No resolutions, composite acyclicity or left exactness of G are assumed.

proof.text: Use rightDerivedPlusSingleUnitHomology_comp_comparison to identify H^0 of u_F(X) with toRightDerivedZero. Left exactness makes this an isomorphism whose inverse is rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf. RF(X) has no negative homology.

By t-structure orthogonality the unit factors uniquely through truncation below 1. Its further truncation at 0 is an isomorphism since RF(X) has no negative homology. The lemma homologyFunctor_map_eTruncLTCompETruncGEIso_hom_app normalizes this identification on H^0, so faithfulness of degree-zero homology on the heart identifies the bottom-interval inclusion with the unit under the H^0 source identification.

Expand grothendieckBottomEdgeSourceIso at q=0. Zero-shift coherence cancels the single-functor, RG and homology shift comparisons; naturality moves the inverse H^0 source identification past the single-object homology comparison for G. Apply RG and H^n to the normalized inclusion. The inverse comparison for G is exactly the remaining source factor.

theorem grothendieckBottomEdge_singleUnit
    {A : Type uA} [Category.{vA} A] [Abelian A] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{vA} A]
    {B : Type uB} [Category.{vB} B] [Abelian B] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{vB} B]
    {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] [Abelian C]
    [HasDerivedCategory A] [HasDerivedCategory B] [HasDerivedCategory C]
    (F : A ⥤ B) (G : B ⥤ C) [F.Additive] [G.Additive]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits F] (X : A) (n : ℕ) :
    (F.grothendieckBottomEdgeSourceIso G n).inv.app X ≫
        (F.grothendieckBottomEdge G n).app X =
      (G.homologyRightDerivedFunctorPlusObjSingleFunctorIso (F.obj X) n).inv ≫
        (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor C n).map
          (G.rightDerivedFunctorPlus.map (F.rightDerivedPlusSingleUnit X))
